items.title: meedee
items.text:
meedee is a Rust MIDI toolkit with Python bindings for sending, receiving, recording and processing MIDI on macOS, Windows and Linux. It supports MIDI 1 and MIDI 2.0/UMP, with tools for playback, routing, SysEx transfers and tuning.

Start with the practical Python examples or practical Rust examples. These examples progress from playing a melody on a synthesizer to recording performances, transferring instrument dumps and discovering MIDI-CI devices.

Browse the API Reference for module, class and function details. For installation and source-build requirements, see the project README.

items.title: Practical Python MIDI examples
items.text:
For the Rust API, see the practical Rust examples.

Start with one note, then work through timing, live input, files and instrument management. Each code block is a separate script. Use Python 3.13 and install with uv sync --locked; the tuning example also needs --extra ufor. See build requirements.

The live examples use the first available port and hard-coded settings. Connect a suitable keyboard or synth before running them. MIDI carries messages, not audio; configure the synth's sound and audio output separately. Channels are 1..16, notes and velocities are 0..127, and program numbers are 1..128.

Inputs and outputs run in-process by default. Use isolated=True for worker failure containment; neither mode requires a main guard. Native MIDI 1 output tracks notes and selected controls for cleanup when explicitly closed or when leaving its context.

items.title: 1. Play one note
items.text:
Play middle C for half a second on the first output.

from meedee.messages import Note
from meedee.midi import Output

with Output() as out:
    out(Note("500 ms", 60))

Note sends both the attack and release. Velocity defaults to 90; the channel comes from the output, which defaults to 1. Use Output(channel=2) to change it.

items.title: 2. Play a tune in beats
items.text:
Set tempo once. Each note or rest advances the tune by its duration.

from meedee.messages import Note, Rest
from meedee.midi import Output

with Output(bpm=120) as out:  # Numeric durations are beats.
    out(
        Note(duration=1, note=60, velocity=90),
        Note(0.5, 62, 70),
        Note(0.5, 64, 100),
        Rest("1 beat"),
        Note(2, 64, 100),
    )

One beat is a quarter note. Without bpm, numeric durations mean seconds. Explicit time units keep their meaning at any tempo; explicit beats require bpm. The clock and scheduling are automatic, without explicit clocks or sleeps.

Output(port="FLOW 8") selects a unique name substring; * and ? support wildcard matching. Input supports the same selection. Two-stage client.connect(client.ports()[0]) returns the same object. Closing is terminal; create a new object to reconnect. For overlapping attacks, use NoteOn with delays and explicit NoteOff releases; Note instead releases before the next item starts. Numeric delays follow the same tempo rule as notes and rests.

Context exit releases outstanding tracked MIDI 1 notes and resets changed pitch bend, modulation, sustain, sostenuto, soft pedal and channel/polyphonic pressure. Volume, pan, expression, programs and tuning are left alone. Reserve the channels for these examples; transport failure can prevent cleanup. UMP requires explicit addressing and does not support these full-note values or automatic cleanup.

items.title: 3. See what your keyboard sends
items.text:
Print messages from the first input. Stop with Ctrl-C.

from meedee.midi import Input

for message in Input():
    print(message)

Iteration yields individual MIDI messages, never Note values. Recoverable input errors are printed to stderr and reception continues; a terminal input failure is reported and ends iteration. Setup, close and output failures still raise. Each message carries optional timestamp, stream and span fields. replace() and transpose() preserve them. Use Input(raw=True) for raw transport packets.

items.title: 4. Transpose a keyboard up an octave
items.text:
Use separate input and output devices to avoid a feedback loop.

from meedee.messages import NoteOff, NoteOn
from meedee.midi import Input, Output

with Input() as input, Output() as output:
    for m in input:
        if isinstance(m, (NoteOn, NoteOff)):
            output(m.transpose(12))
        else:
            output(m)

transpose() returns a new message and clamps the note to 0..127. To handle input diagnostics yourself, use with_errors():

import sys

from meedee.messages import Message, NoteOff, NoteOn
from meedee.midi import Input, Output

with Input() as input, Output() as output:
    for m in input.with_errors():
        if isinstance(m, (NoteOn, NoteOff)):
            output(m.transpose(12))
        elif isinstance(m, Message):
            output(m)
        else:
            print("ERROR", m, file=sys.stderr)

items.title: 5. Split a keyboard into bass and lead
items.text:
Receive channel 1 and split at middle C. Other channel messages, such as sustain and pitch bend, go to both parts.

from meedee.messages import NoteOff, NoteOn, ProgramChange
from meedee.midi import Input, Output

with Input(channel=1) as input, Output() as out:
    out(ProgramChange(34, channel=2))
    out(ProgramChange(81, channel=3))

    for m in input:
        if isinstance(m, (NoteOn, NoteOff)):
            if m.note < 60:
                out(m.replace(channel=2))
            else:
                out(m.replace(channel=3))
        elif getattr(m, "channel", None) is not None:
            out(m.replace(channel=2))
            out(m.replace(channel=3))
        else:
            out(m)

Input(channel=1) selects channel-1 voice messages. A container such as Input(channel=[1, 4]) selects several channels. System messages, including clock and SysEx, pass through and are forwarded once. Diagnostics are always retained. replace() returns a new message.

Alternatively, give each output a channel. An explicitly configured output channel overrides the channel on every MIDI 1 channel message sent through it:

from meedee.messages import NoteOff, NoteOn, ProgramChange
from meedee.midi import Input, Output

with Input() as input, Output(channel=2) as out2, Output(channel=3) as out3:
    out2(ProgramChange(34))
    out3(ProgramChange(81))

    for m in input:
        if isinstance(m, (NoteOn, NoteOff)):
            if m.note < 60:
                out2(m)
            else:
                out3(m)
        elif getattr(m, "channel", None) is not None:
            out2(m)
            out3(m)
        else:
            out2(m)

Use Output() for multiple channels: it preserves assigned message channels and uses channel 1 for unassigned messages. Output(channel=1) explicitly forces channel 1. The override applies to MIDI 1 message objects, full notes and compound commands, including messages sent by play(); encoded packets retain their addressing.

items.title: 6. Record and replay a performance
items.text:
Record ten seconds in memory, then replay it through the first output.

from meedee.midi import Input, Output

Output().play(Input().record(10))

Or save the recording and play it later:

from meedee.archive import Reader
from meedee.midi import Input, Output

filename = "rec.meedee"
Input().record(10, output=filename, overwrite=True)

# Later:
Output().play(Reader(filename))

record() returns messages with their timing and source information, together with archive declarations and any diagnostics. File output writes the same capture; existing files are protected unless overwrite=True. Playback preserves timing between messages and trims initial silence. record() closes its input; the temporary output is finalized after playback. For an output kept in a variable, use a context or explicit close(). play() closes an archive reader.

items.title: 7. Transpose a MIDI file
items.text:
Read song.mid and write song-up.mid, preserving tracks, timing and metadata. Channel 10 is left unchanged under the GM drum convention. This opens no ports.

from pathlib import Path

from meedee import inspection, messages, smf

print(inspection.inspect_file("song.mid", format="smf"))
reader = smf.Reader("song.mid")
try:
    transformed: list[smf.Event] = []
    for event in reader:
        message = event.record
        if isinstance(
            message, (messages.NoteOn, messages.NoteOff, messages.PolyPressure)
        ):
            if message.channel != 10:
                event = event.replace(record=message.replace(note=message.note + 12))
        transformed.append(event)
    with Path("song-up.mid").open("xb") as stream:
        writer = smf.Writer(stream, header=reader.header)
        for event in transformed:
            writer.write(event)
        writer.finish()
finally:
    reader.close()
print(inspection.inspect_file("song-up.mid", format="smf"))

The example holds the file in memory and rejects out-of-range notes before creating the destination. Exclusive creation preserves an existing destination.

items.title: 8. Back up and restore SysEx
items.text:
Start a dump on the instrument after launching this capture script. It expects one complete SysEx message within 30 seconds and creates backup.syx only after successful capture, refusing overwrite. Adjust the count for your instrument.

from meedee import midi, transfer, transfer_input

client = midi.Input(isolated=False)
with client.connect(client.ports()[0]) as receiver:
    capture = transfer.Capture(stream=receiver.stream, expected_messages=1, timeout=30)
    report = transfer_input.run(capture, receiver)
print(report)
if report.status != "completed":
    raise RuntimeError(report.reason)
capture.write("backup.syx")

Run this separate script to restore it. The first output must be the intended instrument, ready to receive this dump: restoration can replace sounds/settings. The 100 ms gap is transfer pacing, not musical timing; use the device's documented requirement. Successful handoff does not prove the device accepted the dump.

from meedee import midi, transfer, transfer_output

plan = transfer.read_file("backup.syx", gap=0.1)
print(plan)
client = midi.Output()
with client.connect(client.ports()[0]) as output:
    print(transfer_output.run(transfer.Session(plan), output))

items.title: 9. Export a just-intonation tuning
items.text:
Create just-three.syx with keys 69, 70 and 71 tuned to 440, 660 and 880 Hz. Install the ufor extra first. The dump targets MTS device ID 0, tuning program 2; unselected keys use NoChange. Send it with the restore example when the receiving synth supports these features and is configured for that device ID.

from pathlib import Path

from ufor.tuning import RatioTable, Tuning

from meedee import codecs, messages, syx, tuning

source = Tuning(source=RatioTable(values=["1", "3/2", "2"]), root_note=69)
pitches = [tuning.convert(source, n) for n in [69, 70, 71]]
print(pitches)
dump = tuning.bulk_dump(
    pitches,
    device_id=0,
    program=2,
    name="Just three",
    preserve_unmapped=True,
)
with Path("just-three.syx").open("xb") as stream:
    syx.write(stream, [messages.SysEx(data=codecs.encode(dump)[1:-1])])

After the instrument has loaded it, select the tuning with output(controls.tuning_program(channel=1, program=2)), importing controls from meedee. Then use the beat-based tune example with notes 69, 70 and 71. MTS program numbers are 0..127, unlike ordinary program changes.

items.title: 10. Bend one note of an MPE chord
items.text:
Hold C and E for two beats, bending only E up two semitones after the first beat. This configures an MPE lower zone on channels 2 and 3 with a 48-semitone bend range. Use an MPE synth and reserve these channels; the configuration remains.

from meedee import controls, events, messages, midi, mpe

zone = mpe.ZoneConfiguration(manager_channel=1, members=2)
allocator = mpe.Allocator(zone=zone)
root = allocator.allocate(note=60, velocity=90)
moving = allocator.allocate(note=64, velocity=75)
bpm = 120
clock = events.Clock(identity="mpe", tick_numerator=60, tick_denominator=bpm)
origin = events.Timestamp(ticks=0, clock=clock)
releases = [allocator.release(voice_id=v.id, velocity=0) for v in [root, moving]]
ending = [*releases, messages.PitchBend(channel=moving.channel, value=0)]
sequence = [
    m.replace(stream="mpe", timestamp=events.Timestamp(ticks=b, clock=clock))
    for b, m in [
        (0, root.note_on),
        (0, moving.note_on),
        (1, messages.PitchBend(channel=moving.channel, value=round(8192 * 2 / 48))),
        *((2, m) for m in ending),
    ]
]
client = midi.Output()
with client.connect(client.ports()[0]) as output:
    output(zone)
    for voice in [root, moving]:
        output(
            controls.pitch_bend_sensitivity(
                channel=voice.channel, semitones=48, cents=0
            )
        )
        output(messages.PitchBend(channel=voice.channel, value=0))
    print(output.play(sequence, origin=origin))

The allocator supplies separate member channels and the corresponding releases. The explicit beat positions here describe expression within a held chord.

items.title: 11. Discover MIDI-CI devices
items.text:
Connect a MIDI-CI device in both directions. This sends Discovery and Product Instance ID inquiries, then prints the complete inventory report. The local identity below is explicitly experimental, using manufacturer ID 0x7D; it does not identify a commercial product. A fresh local MUID is generated for each scan.

from secrets import randbelow

from meedee import ci, ci_live, midi

identity = ci.Identity(
    manufacturer=b"\x7d\x00\x00", family=1, model=1, revision=b"\x00" * 4
)
with midi.Input() as receiver, midi.Output() as output:
    browser = ci.Browser(
        local_muid=randbelow(ci.MAX_MUID + 1),
        identity=identity,
        route=ci.Route(input=receiver.stream, output="device"),
        discovery_timeout=3,
        endpoint_timeout=1,
        timeout=30,
    )
    print(ci_live.run(browser, receiver, output))

The browser handles management replies but performs no Profiles, Property Exchange or instrument configuration writes. An empty inventory does not prove the device is offline. For native UMP, set both clients' protocol to midi.Protocol.Ump and set group=1 on the route; backend support is required.

See the API contract and MIDI-CI contract for ownership, bounds and failure behavior.

items.title: Practical Rust MIDI examples
items.text:
These examples use the meedee Rust crate. Each block is an independent function body; put it inside a function returning Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> and finish with Ok(()). The ? operator propagates a checked error.

Live examples select the first available MIDI port. Connect a keyboard or synth before running them. MIDI carries messages, not audio. Channels are 1..16, notes and velocities are 0..127, and program numbers are 1..128.

items.title: 1. Play one note
items.text:
use meedee::messages::Note;
use meedee::midi::Output;
use std::time::Duration;

Output::new().send(Note::new(Duration::from_millis(500), 60)?)?;

This plays middle C for half a second, with velocity 90 on channel 1. Note sends the attack and release. The temporary output closes when the statement ends.

items.title: 2. Play a tune in beats
items.text:
use meedee::messages::{Beats, Note, Rest};
use meedee::midi::Output;

let mut out = Output::new().with_bpm(120)?;
out.send_all([
    Note::new(Beats::from(1), 60)?.into(),
    Note::new(Beats::new(1, 2)?, 62)?.with_velocity(70)?.into(),
    Note::new(Beats::new(1, 2)?, 64)?.with_velocity(100)?.into(),
    Rest::new(Beats::from(1)).into(),
    Note::new(Beats::from(2), 64)?.into(),
])?;
out.close()?;

One beat is a quarter note; Beats::new(1, 2) is half a beat. Each note or rest advances the sequence. Duration always means elapsed time, even with a tempo; Beats requires a tempo. Clocks and scheduling are automatic. .into() lets notes, rests, messages and delays share one sequence.

Output::new().with_port("FLOW 8")? selects a unique name substring; * and ? also work as wildcards. To choose from discovery, use:

use meedee::midi::Output;

let mut output = Output::new();
let ports = output.ports()?;
println!("{ports:?}");
let mut out = output.connect(&ports[0])?;
out.close()?;

This discovery example assumes there is at least one output. Input supports the same selection methods. The low-level transport module remains available for virtual ports, callbacks and backend-specific settings. Closing is terminal; create a new object to reconnect. Python connect() returns the same object; Rust connect() consumes and returns the resource to express ownership.

items.title: 3. Print incoming messages
items.text:
use meedee::midi::Input;

for message in Input::new() {
    println!("{message:?}");
}

Input yields messages, never full Note values. Malformed traffic and loss are reported on stderr; decoding continues. Terminal connection errors stop the iterator. with_channel(1)? or with_channels([1, 3])? filters channel messages; system messages and diagnostics still pass through.

items.title: 4. Transpose a keyboard
items.text:
use meedee::midi::{Input, Output};
use meedee::events::Payload;
use meedee::messages::AnyMessage;

let mut out = Output::new();
for message in Input::new() {
    match message {
        Payload::Midi1(AnyMessage::NoteOn(note)) => out.send(note.transpose(12))?,
        Payload::Midi1(AnyMessage::NoteOff(note)) => out.send(note.transpose(12))?,
        other => out.send(other)?,
    }
}
out.close()?;

transpose clamps to MIDI's note range and preserves timing/source metadata. Payload distinguishes MIDI 1, UMP and compound commands; AnyMessage identifies the MIDI 1 message kind. These are enums holding the messages themselves, not separate timing wrappers.

items.title: 5. Split a keyboard between two sounds
items.text:
use meedee::midi::{Input, Output};
use meedee::events::Payload;
use meedee::messages::{AnyMessage, ProgramChange};

let mut low = Output::new().with_channel(2)?;
let mut high = Output::new().with_channel(3)?;
low.send(ProgramChange::new(34)?)?;
high.send(ProgramChange::new(81)?)?;

for message in Input::new().with_channel(1)? {
    let key = match &message {
        Payload::Midi1(AnyMessage::NoteOn(note)) => Some(note.note()),
        Payload::Midi1(AnyMessage::NoteOff(note)) => Some(note.note()),
        _ => None,
    };
    match key {
        Some(note) if note < 60 => low.send(message)?,
        Some(_) => high.send(message)?,
        None if matches!(&message, Payload::Midi1(
            AnyMessage::ControlChange(_) | AnyMessage::PolyPressure(_) |
            AnyMessage::ChannelPressure(_) | AnyMessage::ProgramChange(_) |
            AnyMessage::PitchBend(_)
        )) => {
            low.send(message.clone())?;
            high.send(message)?;
        }
        None => low.send(message)?,
    }
}
low.close()?;
high.close()?;

System messages pass through the input filter and are forwarded once. An explicitly configured output channel overrides a MIDI 1 message's channel. Without that setting, an output preserves assigned channels and supplies channel 1 only for unassigned messages. To send several channels through one output, leave its channel unset and use message builders such as .with_channel(2)?.

items.title: 6. Record and replay
items.text:
use meedee::midi::{Input, Output};
use std::time::Duration;

Output::new().play(Input::new().record(Duration::from_secs(10))?)?;

Recording closes the input and returns a Recording containing declarations, messages and any receive problems. Replay infers its origin from the first message. To retain the result, bind it to a variable and print the whole recording.

To save and read the capture:

use meedee::midi::{Input, Output};
use meedee::archive::Reader;
use std::time::Duration;

Input::new().record_to(Duration::from_secs(10), "rec.meedee", true)?;
let report = Output::new().play(Reader::open("rec.meedee")?)?;
println!("{report:?}");

The final true allows overwriting; use false to preserve existing files. Recording retains the capture in memory before writing, so memory use grows with traffic. A disk-write failure can leave a partial file, rejected by the strict reader. Receive errors remain visible as gap/discontinuity records; a structurally complete file does not imply a loss-free performance.

Replay stops at a gap, discontinuity, malformed record, timestamp regression or unmapped clock. Its error includes confirmed progress. Explicit clock mappings, rounding permission, cancellation and metrics are configured with Output::with_playback.

items.title: 7. Handle input diagnostics explicitly
items.text:
use meedee::midi::Input;
use meedee::events::InputItem;

let mut input = Input::new();
for item in input.with_errors() {
    match item? {
        InputItem::Message(message) => println!("{message:?}"),
        InputItem::Diagnostic(diagnostic) => eprintln!("{diagnostic:?}"),
    }
}

The native callback feeds a bounded raw-packet queue. Decoding happens on the calling thread and resets partial state after loss. Queue overflow is reported after the accepted prefix, even if the sender goes silent. Closing also reports remaining native loss and unfinished messages. with_receive_limits configures queue and SysEx limits; with_transport configures backend admission separately.

items.title: 8. Overlap notes and send a compound command
items.text:
use meedee::midi::Output;
use meedee::messages::{NoteOn, RpnSet};
use std::time::Duration;

let mut out = Output::new();
out.send(RpnSet::new(0, 2 << 7)?)?; // Pitch-bend sensitivity: two semitones.
out.send_all([
    NoteOn::new(60)?.into(),
    Duration::from_millis(300).into(),
    NoteOn::new(64)?.into(),
    Duration::from_millis(300).into(),
    NoteOn::new(67)?.into(),
    Duration::from_secs(1).into(),
])?;
out.close()?;

These NoteOn messages overlap until close releases them. Compound commands expand internally. The complete sequence is validated before its first send.

Close releases tracked MIDI 1 note counts and resets changed pitch bend, modulation, sustain, sostenuto, soft pedal and channel/polyphonic pressure. Volume, pan, expression, programs, tuning and other parameters are left alone. The pitch-bend sensitivity set above therefore remains in effect. Drop performs best-effort cleanup; explicit close() returns cleanup errors. Use channels owned by this connection: cleanup can affect another writer sharing a channel, and a failed transport can prevent cleanup.

items.title: 9. Preserve provenance while editing a message
items.text:
use meedee::midi::{Input, Output};
use meedee::events::Payload;
use meedee::messages::{AnyMessage, Message};

let mut out = Output::new();
for message in Input::new() {
    if let Payload::Midi1(AnyMessage::NoteOn(note)) = message {
        let edited = note.with_velocity(70)?.transpose(12);
        println!("{:?}", edited.metadata());
        out.send(edited)?;
        break;
    }
}
out.close()?;

The Message trait exposes optional timestamp, source and packet-span metadata. Builders and transposition preserve it. Equality and hashing compare musical content, ignoring provenance; archive records compare recorded occurrences. Encoding a channel message directly requires an assigned channel. Output resolves an unassigned channel for you.

items.title: 10. Send native MIDI 2 messages
items.text:
use meedee::midi::Output;
use meedee::transport::{OutputOptions, Protocol};
use meedee::ump::{Midi2NoteOff, Midi2NoteOn};
use std::time::Duration;

let mut out = Output::new().with_transport(OutputOptions {
    protocol: Protocol::Ump,
    ..OutputOptions::default()
})?;
out.send_all([
    Midi2NoteOn::new(1, 1, 60, 40_000, 0, 0)?.into(),
    Duration::from_millis(500).into(),
    Midi2NoteOff::new(1, 1, 60, 0, 0, 0)?.into(),
])?;
out.close()?;

This needs a native UMP backend and endpoint. Group and channel are explicit; MIDI 2 velocity uses its native 16-bit range. There is no automatic protocol translation, full-note scheduling or cleanup for UMP. Raw packets likewise retain their own addressing. The ump module provides explicit translation when needed.

items.title: 11. Inspect and compare saved captures
items.text:
These operations open files, not MIDI ports. Reports keep capture quality separate from structural completeness.

use meedee::inspection::{self, ComparisonOptions, Format, Options};

println!("{:?}", inspection::inspect_file("rec.meedee", Format::Archive, &Options::default())?);
println!("{:?}", inspection::compare_files(
    "rec.meedee", "other.meedee", Format::Archive, &ComparisonOptions::default(),
)?);

For playback diagnostics, configure the output once. The options apply to each subsequent play() call; ordinary playback needs no options.

use meedee::archive::Reader;
use meedee::midi::{Output, PlaybackOptions};

let mut out = Output::new().with_playback(PlaybackOptions {
    metrics: true,
    ..Default::default()
});
println!("{:?}", out.play(Reader::open("rec.meedee")?)?);
out.close()?;

PlaybackOptions also accepts an origin timestamp, clock mappings, rounding permission and a shared events::Cancellation. Inspection and metrics snapshots expose read-only getters with the same names as Python properties.

items.title: 12. Capture and restore a SysEx dump
items.text:
Initiate a one-message dump on the instrument within ten seconds. The capture retains complete messages, then creates a new backup file only after success.

use meedee::{midi::Input, transfer, transfer_input};
use std::fs::OpenOptions;

let mut input = Input::new();
let mut capture = transfer::Capture::new(
    input.stream()?.into(), 1, 10_000_000_000, 8_388_608, 1_048_576,
)?;
let report = transfer_input::run(&mut capture, &mut input, None)?;
input.close()?;
println!("{report:?}");
if report.status == "completed" {
    capture.write(&mut OpenOptions::new().write(true).create_new(true).open("backup.syx")?)?;
}

Run this separately to restore the backup. The first output must be the intended instrument, ready to receive it. Sending a dump can replace sounds or settings; choose the gap from the device's documentation.

use meedee::{midi::Output, transfer, transfer_output};
use std::time::Duration;

let plan = transfer::read_file("backup.syx", Duration::from_millis(100), &Default::default())?;
let mut session = transfer::Session::new(plan);
let mut output = Output::new();
println!("{:?}", transfer_output::run(&mut session, &mut output, None)?);
output.close()?;

items.title: 13. Query a tuning dump
items.text:
This asks device 0 for tuning program 2 through the first input/output pair. The final report includes a matching reply, timeout or failure with known progress.

use meedee::{midi::{Input, Output}, tuning, tuning_live};

let mut input = Input::new();
let mut output = Output::new();
let mut query = tuning::Query::new(
    tuning::BulkDumpRequest::new(0, 2)?.into(), input.stream()?.into(), 5_000_000_000,
)?;
println!("{:?}", tuning_live::run(&mut query, &mut input, &mut output, None)?);
input.close()?;
output.close()?;

Live drivers require fresh sessions and own their monotonic clocks. They borrow connections; the caller owns closing them. Failures never trigger automatic retries. High-level I/O errors use midi::Error; native categories and error causes remain available for inspection instead of being flattened into strings.

items.title: 14. Observe endpoint changes
items.text:
Each call performs one complete discovery scan. A failed or oversized scan stops the poller and retains its last complete snapshot.

use meedee::{discovery::Poller, midi::Protocol};

let mut poller = Poller::new(Protocol::Midi1)?;
println!("{:?}", poller.poll()?);
// Call poll() again when the application wants another observation.
poller.close();

Python additionally provides process isolation, CLI commands, unit strings and uFor integration. Rust uses typed durations, builders, enums and Result values; its transport and file_io modules expose lower-level native and streaming primitives. Corresponding workflows otherwise use the same public module names.

items.title: 15. Discover MIDI-CI devices
items.text:
This uses the experimental manufacturer identity 0x7D and a caller-selected local MUID. Choose a fresh unused MUID for a real scan. Python's example generates one with secrets; Rust leaves that choice to the application's random-number source.

use meedee::{ci, ci_live, midi::{Input, Output}};

let mut input = Input::new();
let mut output = Output::new();

A group-less route uses MIDI 1 bytes; an explicit group uses UMP SysEx7. Full-action handoffs are counted, and a partial/interrupted action is uncertain.

def run(
    browser: ci.Browser,
    receiver: midi.Input,
    output: midi.Output,
    *,
    cancel: events.Cancellation | None = None,
    message_limit: int = 1_048_576,
    byte_limit: int = 8_388_608,
) -> ci.BrowseReport:
    """Run a fresh browser; callers own connections and serialize all access.

    A group-less route uses MIDI 1 bytes; an explicit group uses UMP SysEx7.
    Full-action handoffs are counted, and a partial/interrupted action is uncertain.
    """
    from . import midi

    route = browser.route
    if route.input != receiver.stream:
        raise ValueError("browser route must match the receiver stream")
    assembler = ump.EventAssembler(
        message_limit=message_limit, total_limit=byte_limit, max_streams=1
    )
    queue: deque[ci.Action] = deque()
    sending: int | None = None
    try:
        queue.extend(browser.start(monotonic_ns()))
        while browser.snapshot().status in ("discovering", "inquiring", "stopping"):
            if cancel is not None and cancel.cancelled:
                browser.stop("cancelled by caller")
                break
            if receiver.dropped_packets:
                browser.stop("input packet loss reported by transport counter")
                break
            if (error := receiver.failure) is not None:
                raise error
            queue.extend(browser.poll(monotonic_ns()))
            pending = browser.snapshot().pending_tokens
            queue = deque(a for a in queue if a.token in pending)
            if queue:
                action = queue.popleft()
                if route.group is None:
                    packets: list[messages.Message] = [action.message]
                else:
                    wire = codecs.encode(action.message)
                    packets = list(
                        ump.packetize_sysex7(group=route.group, data=wire[1:-1])
                    )
                for packet in packets:
                    if receiver.dropped_packets or receiver.failure is not None:
                        raise midi.WorkerError(
                            "input failed or lost packets during management send"
                        )
                    if cancel is not None and cancel.cancelled:
                        raise KeyboardInterrupt
                    sending = action.token
                    output(packet)
                queue.extend(
                    browser.report_send(
                        token=action.token, sent=True, now_ns=monotonic_ns()
                    )
                )
                sending = None
                continue
            if browser.snapshot().status not in ("discovering", "inquiring"):
                continue
            item = receiver.receive(timeout=0.05)
            if item is None:
                continue
            if isinstance(item, events.StreamDiagnostic):
                assembler.reset()
                browser.stop(item.reason)
                break
            if item.stream != route.input:
                browser.stop("received event from an unrelated stream")
                break
            if route.group is None:
                if isinstance(item, messages.SysEx):
                    queue.extend(
                        browser.feed(item, input=route.input, now_ns=monotonic_ns())
                    )
            elif isinstance(item, ump.SysEx7Packet) and item.group == route.group:
                for observation in assembler.feed(item):
                    value = observation.value
                    if isinstance(value, ump.AssembledData):
                        queue.extend(
                            browser.feed(
                                messages.SysEx(data=value.data),
                                input=route.input,
                                group=route.group,
                                now_ns=monotonic_ns(),
                            )
                        )
                    else:
                        browser.stop("UMP SysEx7 assembly diagnostic: " + str(value))
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        if sending is not None and sending in browser.snapshot().pending_tokens:
            browser.report_send(token=sending, sent=False, now_ns=monotonic_ns())
            sending = None
        browser.stop("interrupted")
    except (
        midi.MidiError,
        midi.StateError,
        midi.CallbackThreadError,
        midi.NativePanicError,
        midi.ResourceError,
        midi.WorkerError,
        midi.WorkerTimeoutError,
        OSError,
        ValueError,
    ) as error:
        if sending is not None and sending in browser.snapshot().pending_tokens:
            browser.report_send(token=sending, sent=False, now_ns=monotonic_ns())
            sending = None
        browser.stop(str(error))
        raise
    finally:
        if sending is not None and sending in browser.snapshot().pending_tokens:
            browser.report_send(token=sending, sent=False, now_ns=monotonic_ns())
        assembler.reset()
        if browser.snapshot().status in ("discovering", "inquiring", "stopping"):
            browser.stop("scan did not complete")
    return browser.snapshot()

def run(
    capture: transfer.Capture,
    receiver: midi.Input,
    *,
    cancel: events.Cancellation | None = None,
) -> transfer.CaptureReport:
    """Run a fresh capture; callers own the connection and serialize access.

    Uses the supplied input's existing decoder. No requests, retries or cleanup
    traffic are sent. The capture deadline starts here, after connection setup.
    Receive waits are at most 50 ms; an in-process driver stall remains unbounded.
    """
    from . import midi

    capture.start(monotonic_ns())
    try:
        while capture.snapshot().status == "active":
            if cancel is not None and cancel.cancelled:
                capture.cancel("cancelled by caller")
                break
            if receiver.dropped_packets:
                capture.fail("input packet loss reported by transport counter")
                break
            if (error := receiver.failure) is not None:
                raise error
            now = monotonic_ns()
            capture.poll(now)
            report = capture.snapshot()
            if report.status != "active":
                break
            assert report.deadline_ns is not None
            item = receiver.receive(
                timeout=min(0.05, (report.deadline_ns - now) / 1_000_000_000)
            )
            if receiver.dropped_packets:
                capture.fail("input packet loss reported by transport counter")
                break
            if (error := receiver.failure) is not None:
                raise error
            if cancel is not None and cancel.cancelled:
                capture.cancel("cancelled by caller")
                break
            if item is not None:
                capture.feed(item, monotonic_ns())
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        capture.cancel("interrupted")
    except (
        midi.MidiError,
        midi.StateError,
        midi.CallbackThreadError,
        midi.NativePanicError,
        midi.ResourceError,
        midi.WorkerError,
        midi.WorkerTimeoutError,
        OSError,
        ValueError,
    ) as error:
        capture.fail(str(error))
    finally:
        if capture.snapshot().status == "active":
            capture.fail("capture did not complete")
    return capture.snapshot()

def run(
    session: transfer.Session,
    output: midi.Output,
    *,
    cancel: events.Cancellation | None = None,
) -> transfer.Report:
    """Run until terminal; never close the caller's output or retry a send.

    The caller supplies a MIDI 1 connection. Cancellation is checked at most every
    50 ms while waiting, but cannot interrupt an in-flight native send. Unexpected
    exceptions propagate; the caller can inspect the supplied session afterward.
    """
    from . import midi

    initial = session.snapshot()
    if (
        initial.status != "active"
        or initial.confirmed_messages
        or initial.in_flight is not None
    ):
        raise ValueError("transfer session must be fresh")
    cancel = events.Cancellation() if cancel is None else cancel
    try:
        while session.snapshot().status == "active":
            if cancel is not None and cancel.cancelled:
                session.cancel("cancelled by caller")
                break
            now = monotonic_ns()
            step = session.prepare(now)
            if step is None:
                deadline = session.snapshot().next_ready_ns
                assert deadline is not None
                cancel.wait_for(min(0.05, max(0, deadline - now) / 1_000_000_000))
                continue
            try:
                output(step.message)
            except (
                midi.MidiError,
                midi.StateError,
                midi.CallbackThreadError,
                midi.NativePanicError,
                midi.ResourceError,
                midi.WorkerError,
                midi.WorkerTimeoutError,
                OSError,
                ValueError,
            ) as error:
                session.fail(step.index, str(error))
                break
            session.confirm(step.index, monotonic_ns())
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        session.cancel("interrupted")
    finally:
        if (index := session.snapshot().in_flight) is not None:
            session.fail(index, "send or confirmation did not complete")
    return session.snapshot()

def convert(source: Tuning, note: int) -> tuning.NoteTuning:
    """Convert one source note to MTS; raise KeyError outside finite coverage."""
    from ufor.tuning import Tuning

    if not isinstance(source, Tuning):
        raise TypeError("source must be a uFor Tuning")
    _check_notes([note])
    if not _covered(source, note):
        raise KeyError(f"note {note} is outside the finite uFor tuning")
    frequency = source(note)
    if isinstance(frequency, float) and not isfinite(frequency):
        raise ValueError("uFor resolved a non-finite frequency")
    if frequency <= 0:
        raise ValueError("uFor resolved a non-positive frequency")
    minimum = tuning.Pitch(semitone=0, fraction=0).frequency_hz
    maximum = tuning.Pitch(semitone=127, fraction=16382).frequency_hz
    # Compare exact values before float conversion can round onto an endpoint.
    if not minimum <= frequency <= maximum:
        raise ValueError("frequency is outside meedee's MTS frequency range")
    pitch = tuning.Pitch.from_frequency(frequency_hz=float(frequency)).pitch
    return tuning.NoteTuning(note=note, pitch=pitch)

def bulk_dump(
    result: list[tuning.NoteTuning],
    *,
    device_id: int,
    program: int,
    name: str,
    bank: int | None = None,
    preserve_unmapped: bool = False,
) -> tuning.BulkDump | tuning.KeyBasedDump:
    """Build an ordinary or banked 128-key dump. Never open a port or send."""
    changes = _changes(result, preserve_unmapped)
    if len(changes) != 128 and not preserve_unmapped:
        raise ValueError("bulk dumps require all 128 keys or explicit preservation")
    values: list[tuning.Pitch | tuning.NoChange] = [
        tuning.NoChange() for _ in range(128)
    ]
    for change in changes:
        values[change.note] = change.pitch
    table = tuning.TuningTable(values=values)
    if bank is None:
        return tuning.BulkDump(
            device_id=device_id, program=program, name=name, table=table
        )
    return tuning.KeyBasedDump(
        device_id=device_id, bank=bank, program=program, name=name, table=table
    )

def run(
    query: tuning.Query,
    receiver: midi.Input,
    output: midi.Output,
    *,
    cancel: events.Cancellation | None = None,
) -> tuning.QueryReport:
    """Send once, then receive until terminal. Never close connections or retry.

    The caller supplies one MIDI 1 queued input and output. Existing queued input
    is eligible: MTS has no transaction ID to disambiguate an identical old dump.
    """
    from . import midi

    if query.snapshot().status != "ready":
        raise ValueError("query must be fresh")
    try:
        while query.snapshot().status in ("ready", "waiting"):
            if cancel is not None and cancel.cancelled:
                query.cancel("cancelled by caller")
                break
            if receiver.dropped_packets:
                query.fail("input packet loss reported by transport counter")
                break
            if (error := receiver.failure) is not None:
                raise error
            now = monotonic_ns()
            if query.snapshot().status == "ready":
                request = query.prepare(now)
                output(request)
                query.confirm(monotonic_ns())
                continue
            query.poll(now)
            report = query.snapshot()
            if report.status != "waiting":
                break
            assert report.deadline_ns is not None
            item = receiver.receive(
                timeout=min(0.05, (report.deadline_ns - now) / 1_000_000_000)
            )
            if receiver.dropped_packets:
                query.fail("input packet loss reported by transport counter")
                break
            if (error := receiver.failure) is not None:
                raise error
            if cancel is not None and cancel.cancelled:
                query.cancel("cancelled by caller")
                break
            if item is not None:
                query.feed(item, monotonic_ns())
    except KeyboardInterrupt:
        query.cancel("interrupted")
    except (
        midi.MidiError,
        midi.StateError,
        midi.CallbackThreadError,
        midi.NativePanicError,
        midi.ResourceError,
        midi.WorkerError,
        midi.WorkerTimeoutError,
        OSError,
        ValueError,
    ) as error:
        query.fail(str(error))
    finally:
        if query.snapshot().status in ("ready", "sending", "waiting"):
            query.fail("query did not complete")
    return query.snapshot()
